content.user_title: Build Rust MCP Servers with rmcp
content.value_statement: Rust developers need a direct path from MCP concepts to a working server. This skill explains rmcp setup, service patterns, transports, tests, and debugging steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains MCP tools, resources, prompts, and transport choices.
Shows how to add rmcp, Tokio, serde, schemars, and thiserror dependencies.
Provides a complete Hello World MCP server pattern in Rust.
Describes stdio, SSE, and HTTP streaming transport options.
Covers unit tests, integration tests, logging, and common rmcp debugging issues.
limitations: It is a guide, not an installed Rust project or runnable server.
Version notes may need confirmation against the current rmcp release.
It does not cover production authentication, authorization, or deployment hardening in depth.
It assumes the user already has a Rust toolchain and basic async Rust knowledge.

use_cases.title: Create a First MCP Server
use_cases.description: Follow a simple rmcp pattern to create tools, choose stdio transport, and test local behavior.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Transport Options
use_cases.description: Compare stdio, SSE, and HTTP streaming for local tools, cloud services, and web deployments.
use_cases.target_user: Backend engineer planning an MCP integration

use_cases.title: Debug rmcp Tool Definitions
use_cases.description: Check macro usage, parameter types, async functions, tests, and logging when tools fail to appear.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create my first rmcp MCP server in Rust. Explain the project structure, dependencies, and the smallest useful tool.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Transport
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare stdio, SSE, and HTTP streaming for my rmcp server. Recommend one for local development and one for deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Add Typed Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding an rmcp tool with structured parameters, validation, and useful error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Server Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my planned rmcp server architecture for tool boundaries, async state handling, testing strategy, and deployment risks.

output_examples.input: Help me build a basic rmcp server with one greeting tool.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan covering Cargo setup, required dependencies, service structure, tool macro usage, and local test commands.

output_examples.input: My rmcp tool is not visible to the client.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist that reviews tool descriptions, tool_box placement, async signatures, supported return types, and test coverage.

output_examples.input: Should I use stdio or HTTP streaming for my MCP server?
output_examples.output: A transport recommendation based on local use, remote access needs, deployment environment, and expected client behavior.

best_practices: Start with one small tool and verify it with tests before adding resources or prompts.
Use clear tool descriptions and typed parameters so clients can call tools safely.
Confirm rmcp and MCP specification versions before copying dependency versions into production.
anti_patterns: Do not expose broad filesystem, network, or shell access in a first MCP server.
Do not skip tests for tool behavior, parameter validation, and server lifecycle handling.
Do not choose a remote transport before defining authentication and deployment boundaries.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build a basic Rust MCP server with rmcp and understand the main development workflow.

faq.question: Does this skill install rmcp automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You choose when to edit dependencies and run Cargo commands.

faq.question: Which transports does it explain?
faq.answer: It explains stdio for local use, SSE for cloud use, and HTTP streaming for web-style deployments.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers unit tests for tools, integration test ideas, and common debugging checks.

faq.question: Is this only for experienced Rust developers?
faq.answer: No. It is beginner friendly, but basic Rust and async concepts will make the guide easier to use.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
